company.name: Dian Xiaomi
company.shortDescription: Dian Xiaomi provides one-stop services for global e-commerce sellers.
company.description:
Dian Xiaomi is a e-commerce IT service company, focusing on providing SaaS system services for global e-commerce sellers, making it easier to "buy and sell globally".

Dian Xiaomi gathers a strong domestic IT R&D team. The core members are from well-known companies such as Baidu, Tencent, and Meituan. They have 15+ years of experience in software research and development.

Dian Xiaomi was established on March 26, 2014 by Jianyin Du in Longgang, Guangdong.

aiResearchSummary.text: Dian Xiaomi is engaged in developing systems and methods for e-commerce sellers, focusing on areas such as commodity publishing based on image batch processing, customer service information generation from historical conversations, multi-platform commodity release, e-commerce promotion management, overseas warehouse procurement, and accounts receivable data processing. Their research also covers logistics information generation, early warning systems for operations and freight, and cross-platform data management, supporting comprehensive e-commerce operations and seller services.

insights.title: Funding is concentrated in the latest major round
insights.statement: The latest disclosed Series D round raised $110,000,000, or 43.1% of reported total funding.
insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.

insights.title: Valuation increased across disclosed rounds
insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $4,930,837 to $1,011,721,645, a 205.18x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.

insights.statement: Crunchbase scores growth at 56 (+0 over 90 days) and market heat at 51 (-8).
insights.implication: The company has recently become much more visible, but the scores should be treated as attention/activity indicators rather than revenue or clinical-performance metrics.
